question.text: GST is applicable on which of the following components of trading costs in ETIRD?

answer.text: Brokerage, exchange charges, and other service charges

explanation.text: The Logic: GST is a tax on the supply of services, and trading-related charges in ETIRD are service-fee components. Under the GST law, brokerage charged by the trading member, exchange transaction charges, clearing charges, and any other service charges levied by intermediaries on the client are all treated as taxable services. As a result, GST applies on these service components — not just on one of them — at the prevailing service rate, increasing the total cost of an ETIRD trade. The Trap: "Only brokerage" and "Only exchange charges" each pick a single service component, but in practice GST is charged on the full bundle of service components. "None — ETIRD is GST exempt" is also wrong; while STT does not apply to interest rate derivatives, GST does apply to the service charges levied on the trade. Note: The cited NISM Series IV Interest Rate Derivatives workbook pages reviewed in the audit identify GST as a statutory levy and separately list exchange/regulatory charges and brokerage as items that can be charged to a client, but do not state on the pages checked that GST applies across brokerage + exchange charges + other service charges as a combined base. The framing above reflects general industry practice and the GST law's treatment of service fees.
